ladakh_high_altitude.name: Ladakh & Western Himalayas (High Altitude Cold Desert)
ladakh_high_altitude.description: High diurnal swing, sub-zero winters (-20°C), intense solar irradiance (>750 W/m²), high UV, transport passes closed in winter.

arctic_subzero.name: Arctic & Sub-Zero Tundra (Extreme Polar Cold)
arctic_subzero.description: Prolonged extreme sub-zero conditions (-35°C), low winter solar gains, permafrost ground, high wind chill.

hot_arid_desert.name: Thar & Arabian Desert (Hot Arid)
hot_arid_desert.description: Severe daytime heat (>45°C), strong diurnal drop, high solar radiation, sandstorms, scarce water.

tropical_humid.name: Coastal & Western Ghats (Tropical Humid)
tropical_humid.description: High ambient humidity (>80%), high rainfall, moderate-high temperatures (30-36°C), mold/rot hazard.

temperate_alpine.name: Shimla & Mid-Himalayan Alpine (Temperate Alpine)
temperate_alpine.description: Moderate seasonal shifts, freezing snow winter, pleasant summer, rainfall during monsoon.

global_standard.name: Standard Continental (Temperate)
global_standard.description: Balanced heating and cooling degree days, standard urban supply chains.

humanitarian_low.label: Humanitarian / Low Cost ($)
humanitarian_low.description: Prioritizes locally sourced, low-cost or earth-based materials.

moderate_balanced.label: Moderate / Cost-Effective ($$)
moderate_balanced.description: Balances thermal efficiency with standard commercial affordability.

premium_high_perf.label: High-Performance / Premium ($$$)
premium_high_perf.description: Maximizes passive performance, durability, and specialized insulation.

normal_weight_concrete.name: Normal-weight concrete
advantages: Very high volumetric heat capacity (2.02 MJ/m³·K) for passive thermal mass
Exceptional structural durability, compressive strength, and lifespan (80+ yrs)
Impervious to rodent intrusion and rot; class A1 non-combustible
disadvantages: High thermal conductivity (1.7 W/m·K) requires exterior insulation wrap
Heavy transport penalty (2300 kg/m³) on high-altitude passes
High embodied carbon footprint

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / NIST reference data

high_strength_concrete.name: High-strength concrete
advantages: Maximum compressive strength for multistory or heavy seismic loads
Superior freeze-thaw cracking resistance in sub-zero environments
Dense thermal mass
disadvantages: Very high thermal conductivity (2.0 W/m·K) causes severe thermal bridging without insulation
Requires specialized batching plants rarely available in remote mountain valleys

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / engineering reference

aerated_autoclaved_concrete_aac.name: Aerated autoclaved concrete (AAC)
advantages: Low thermal conductivity (0.12 W/m·K) provides integrated structural insulation
Lightweight (550 kg/m³) reduces dead load and logistics transport effort
Excellent fire resistance and acoustic absorption
disadvantages: Hydrophilic porous matrix requires breathable external waterproofing against freeze-thaw spalling
Lower thermal mass than dense concrete or stone

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / engineering reference

dense_concrete_block.name: Dense concrete block
advantages: Inexpensive and widely manufactured
Decent thermal mass (1.76 MJ/m³·K)
Robust against physical abrasion and pests
disadvantages: Moderate thermal conductivity (1.1 W/m·K) needs continuous external insulation
Mortar joints can create thermal bridges if uninsulated

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / NIST reference data

lightweight_concrete_block.name: Lightweight concrete block
advantages: Balanced weight and thermal conductivity (0.3 W/m·K)
Easier manual handling during emergency shelter erection
disadvantages: Lower structural compressive capacity
Requires moisture protection in freeze zones

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / NIST reference data

common_clay_brick.name: Common clay brick
advantages: Time-tested construction material with proven thermal inertia
High solar absorptivity (0.71) helpful for passive solar facade heating
Good durability and fire resistance
disadvantages: Substantial thermal transmission (0.6 W/m·K) requires supplemental insulation in extreme cold
Labor-intensive wet masonry construction

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / NIST reference data

engineering_brick.name: Engineering brick
advantages: Extremely low water absorption (<4.5%), immune to freeze-thaw frost heave
High density and compressive capacity
disadvantages: High thermal conductivity (1.1 W/m·K)
Heavier and higher cost than standard clay brick

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / engineering reference

adobe_mud_brick.name: Adobe / mud brick
advantages: Outstanding local availability in Ladakh and arid valleys using indigenous silt/soil
Near-zero embodied carbon and very low construction budget
High thermal mass (1.44 MJ/m³·K) ideal for diurnal phase-shift damping
Naturally regulates indoor relative humidity via hygroscopic buffering
disadvantages: Vulnerable to water erosion and driving rains; needs lime plaster or wide roof overhangs
Requires thicker walls (300-450mm) to achieve adequate thermal resistance

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: Building-material literature / engineering reference

granite.name: Granite
advantages: Virtually indestructible stone with 100+ year lifespan; impervious to freeze-thaw cycles
Abundantly quarryable on-site across Himalayan slopes and Ladakh ranges
High thermal mass (2.13 MJ/m³·K) serves as a supreme heat sink when wrapped with exterior insulation
disadvantages: Extremely high thermal conductivity (2.8 W/m·K) — UNUSABLE without external insulation wrap
Heavy manual stone masonry requires skilled labor

limestone.name: Limestone
advantages: Lower thermal conductivity than granite (1.3 W/m·K)
High thermal mass (2.07 MJ/m³·K)
Workable stone with attractive aesthetic
disadvantages: Susceptible to acid precipitation and freeze-thaw micro-fissuring in wet climates

sandstone.name: Sandstone
advantages: Good thermal storage (1.76 MJ/m³·K)
Readily split into flat slabs for flooring and walls in arid zones
disadvantages: Higher porosity than granite requires sealant against water penetration in freezing conditions

marble.name: Marble
advantages: High thermal effusivity (cool to touch in hot climates)
High scratch and compressive resistance
disadvantages: Poor thermal insulator (2.9 W/m·K); feels cold in sub-zero winters
High financial cost

slate.name: Slate
advantages: Extremely durable pitched roofing material; resists severe mountain snow loads and freeze-thaw
Natural cleavage provides impermeable water-shedding tiles
disadvantages: Heavy roof framing required (2700 kg/m³)
High thermal transmission requires thick attic/rafter insulation underneath

gypsum_plaster.name: Gypsum plaster
advantages: Smooth interior air-tight finish reduces unintended infiltration
Endothermic water release during fire exposure
disadvantages: Strictly interior only; rapidly breaks down if exposed to exterior moisture

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: NIST reference / building-material literature

gypsum_board.name: Gypsum board
advantages: Fast dry installation with stud framing
Low thermal conductivity (0.16 W/m·K) assists internal comfort
disadvantages: Susceptible to moisture damage unless treated with greenboard/cement backer

cement_plaster.name: Cement plaster
advantages: Tough external weather barrier protecting masonry from driving snow and wind
Good impact resistance
disadvantages: Vapor-impermeable compared to lime; can trap internal condensation if incorrectly placed

lime_plaster.name: Lime plaster
advantages: Vapor-permeable ('breathable') finish essential for adobe, rammed earth, and straw-bale envelopes
Self-healing microcracks via carbonation; natural antiseptic/antifungal qualities
disadvantages: Slower setting and curing time in cold weather

ceramic_tile.name: Ceramic tile
advantages: Waterproof, abrasion-resistant, easy to sanitize
Good thermal coupling with underfloor radiant heating or solar direct gain
disadvantages: High thermal effusivity feels cold to bare feet without insulation layer underneath

hardwood_timber.name: Hardwood timber
advantages: Carbon-sequestering renewable material
Low thermal conductivity (0.18 W/m·K) prevents cold bridging
High specific heat (1600 J/kg·K) creates comfortable interior touch warmth
disadvantages: Extremely scarce in high-altitude desert (Ladakh is above tree line; requires transport)
Vulnerable to termite attack in humid tropics unless treated

plywood.name: Plywood
advantages: Shear diaphragms for seismic stability and roof decking
Low thermal conductivity (0.13 W/m·K)
disadvantages: Standard grades delaminate if soaked; requires marine or exterior grade adhesive

osb_board.name: OSB board
advantages: Cost-effective structural sheathing
Consistent structural properties without natural knot defects
disadvantages: Edge swelling under prolonged water exposure

cork_board.name: Cork board
advantages: 100% natural, renewable, carbon-negative insulation (k=0.043 W/m·K)
Naturally impermeable to water and rot; does not off-gas toxic fumes
High specific heat capacity (1800 J/kg·K) provides thermal lag unmatched by petrochemical foams
disadvantages: Higher unit price than EPS or glass fiber
Limited supply chain in Central Asia and remote mountain regions

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: NIST SRD 81 / building-material literature

expanded_perlite.name: Expanded perlite
advantages: Inorganic volcanic glass loose-fill; 100% fireproof and rodent-proof
Decent thermal insulation (k=0.05 W/m·K) for filling masonry cavity cores
disadvantages: Dusty during installation; settles over time if improperly retained

vermiculite.name: Vermiculite
advantages: High thermal stability up to 1200°C; non-combustible
Effective loose-fill for chimneys and thermal ceiling plenums
disadvantages: Slightly higher thermal conductivity (0.065 W/m·K) than modern batt insulations

glass_fiber_batt.name: Glass fiber batt
advantages: Highly affordable thermal insulation (k=0.04 W/m·K)
Lightweight (20 kg/m³) minimal freight payload for high-altitude transport
Non-combustible
disadvantages: Loses insulating ability dramatically if penetrated by condensation or moisture
Requires PPE during handling; can sag if not mechanically supported

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / NIST SRD 81

rock_wool_batt.name: Rock wool batt
advantages: Exceptional low thermal conductivity (0.035 W/m·K) providing R-2.86 per 100mm
Melting point >1000°C provides world-class fire barrier in emergency shelters
Vapor-permeable and hydrophobic; sheds water and does not rot or promote mold
Higher density (45 kg/m³) provides superior acoustic insulation and sag resistance
disadvantages: Heavier and slightly more expensive than glass wool

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / NIST SRD 81

cellular_glass.name: Cellular glass
advantages: 100% closed glass cells; totally impervious to water, water vapor, and sub-surface frost
High compressive strength allows load-bearing installation directly under concrete slabs
Rodent, pest, and acid proof
disadvantages: Higher thermal conductivity (0.05 W/m·K) than foam
Brittle; requires careful handling on rough terrain

polyurethane_foam.name: Polyurethane foam
advantages: Superior thermal resistance (k=0.025 W/m·K) — thin profile saves precious shelter interior space
Spray-applied formulation creates seamless air-tight envelope sealing gaps and drafts
disadvantages: Combustible and releases toxic cyanide gases during fire exposure; must be shielded behind drywall
Sensitive to UV degradation if exposed to sunlight

polyisocyanurate_foam.name: Polyisocyanurate foam
advantages: Market-leading thermal resistance (k=0.023 W/m·K) — delivers R-4.35 per 100mm
Often foil-faced to provide radiant heat reflection and vapor barrier in one layer
disadvantages: Conductivity degrades slightly at sub-zero temperatures (blowing gas condensation)
High embodied petrochemical content

phenolic_foam.name: Phenolic foam
advantages: Lowest thermal conductivity among rigid foams (k=0.020 W/m·K)
Superior fire and smoke performance compared to standard polyurethane
disadvantages: Acidic leaching risk if saturated with water in contact with structural metals
Premium pricing

hemp_lime_hempcrete.name: Hemp-lime (hempcrete)
advantages: Carbon-negative composite combining thermal insulation (0.07 W/m·K) and thermal inertia
Volumetric heat capacity of 450 kJ/m³·K moderates temperature swings
Naturally vapor-permeable and mold-inhibiting lime matrix; pest resistant
disadvantages: Non-load-bearing; requires timber or bamboo framing cage
Slow drying in cold humid conditions

sheep_wool_insulation.name: Sheep wool insulation
advantages: Highly available across Ladakh, Changthang nomads, and pastoral Himalayan communities
Low thermal conductivity (k=0.04 W/m·K) equivalent to commercial mineral wool
Can absorb up to 33% of its weight in water vapor without losing thermal resistance
Releases latent heat of adsorption when absorbing moisture in freezing winter nights
disadvantages: Must be treated with borate salts against moth and beetle larvae
Requires light framing retainers

wood_fiber_insulation_board.name: Wood fiber insulation board
advantages: Very high specific heat capacity (2100 J/kg·K) creates 10-12 hr summer heat wave phase lag
Breathable and hygroscopic
Low thermal conductivity (0.045 W/m·K)
disadvantages: Heavier than synthetic foams (160 kg/m³)
Requires weather-resistive barrier

cellulose_loose_fill.name: Cellulose loose-fill
advantages: Recycled paper product with very low embodied carbon
Tight dense packing stops convective air loops inside wall cavities
Affordable thermal performance (k=0.04 W/m·K)
disadvantages: Requires blown-in blowing machine or careful manual tamp
Can settle over 5-10 years if under-compacted

coconut_coir_fiber.name: Coconut coir fiber
advantages: Supreme local availability in coastal, South Asian, and tropical environments
Naturally high lignin content provides resistance to rot and fungal attack
Good thermal insulation (k=0.045 W/m·K)
disadvantages: High freight cost if transported to high mountain altitudes

polyethylene.name: Polyethylene
advantages: Lightweight emergency vapor retarder and greenhouse glazing for solar trombe gain
Inexpensive and instantly deployed
disadvantages: Degrades rapidly under harsh high-altitude UV radiation unless UV-stabilized
Poor thermal resistance without multi-layer dead air cavities

pvc.name: PVC
advantages: Waterproof roofing membranes and window frame profiles
Low maintenance
disadvantages: Becomes brittle in sub-zero extreme cold (-20°C)

rubber.name: Rubber
advantages: EPDM rubber membranes provide supreme flat-roof waterproofing down to -45°C
High elongation accommodates thermal movement
disadvantages: Dark color absorbs high solar heat in summer unless coated with reflective acrylic

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: NIST SRD 81 / engineering reference

glass.name: Glass
advantages: Allows direct passive solar gain into living areas during sunlit hours
Durable surface impervious to scratching and weather
disadvantages: Single-pane has atrocious thermal conductivity (1.0 W/m·K) causing massive nighttime heat drain
Severe condensation and frost formation in winter

provenance.thermal_properties: Measured benchmark: ASHRAE Ch.26 / NIST reference

double_glazing_air_gap.name: Double glazing, air gap
advantages: Cuts window heat loss by ~50% compared to single pane
Reduces interior draft chills and condensation
disadvantages: Seal failure over decades can cause internal fogging
Fragile transport over bumpy unpaved mountain roads

low_e_double_glazing.name: Low-E double glazing
advantages: Microscopic metal coating reflects long-wave infrared heat back into the shelter
Cuts nocturnal radiant heat loss by >70% while admitting 75% of solar daylight
Essential for achieving net-positive solar gain envelopes in sub-zero climates
disadvantages: Higher capital investment
Requires specialized procurement and careful handling

air_gap_still.name: Air gap, still
advantages: Free insulating air barrier (k=0.026 W/m·K) when unventilated and sealed under 25mm thickness
Breaks conductive bridging across masonry wythes
disadvantages: Convective loops degrade performance if gap exceeds 30mm; must be airtight

water.name: Water
advantages: Unrivaled volumetric heat capacity (4.18 MJ/m³·K) — 2x higher than concrete and 4x higher than brick
Thermal drum walls absorb massive solar gain on south glazing and discharge warmth all night long
Virtually free storage medium
disadvantages: Requires freeze protection (glycol or salt) if shelter interior drops below 0°C
Risk of container puncture or leaks over decades

paraffin_pcm.name: Paraffin PCM
advantages: Isothermal latent heat release near human comfort zone (21°C) prevents indoor overheating and freezing
Stores 155 kJ/kg latent enthalpy in a compact lightweight panel
disadvantages: High material cost; low liquid thermal conductivity requires heat-spreader fins

salt_hydrate_pcm_cacl2_6h2o.name: Salt-hydrate PCM (CaCl2·6H2O)
advantages: High latent heat (190 kJ/kg) and higher thermal conductivity than organic paraffin (0.5 W/m·K)
Non-combustible
disadvantages: Phase segregation and subcooling over thousands of freeze-thaw cycles without nucleating agents

eutectic_pcm_organic.name: Eutectic PCM, organic
advantages: Sharp congruent melting with negligible subcooling for precise indoor temperature stabilization
disadvantages: High cost and limited availability in frontier logistics networks

aluminum.name: Aluminum
advantages: Ultra-lightweight (2700 kg/m³) corrosion-resistant roofing sheet
High solar reflectance (0.7) and low emissivity (0.2) acts as radiant heat barrier
disadvantages: Extreme thermal conductivity (205 W/m·K) requires robust continuous insulation underneath to avoid thermal short-circuits

steel.name: Steel
advantages: Pre-fabricated corrugated GI roofing sheets allow rapid emergency weather sealing
High structural wind and snow load resistance
disadvantages: High thermal transmission (50 W/m·K) and condensation drippage without thermal break insulation
